title: Bent.ch
titleFull: Bent.ch, a curved bench | Phào Design
description: A bench with a seat curved to 120 degrees, encouraging an upright posture and short rests. Exhibited at SEE+ Design Fair 2023.
summary: A bench with a seat curved to 120 degrees, holding the sitter upright and encouraging a short rest rather than a long stay.

heroAlt: The Bent.ch plywood bench with its curved seat

chapters.heading: The name
body: Bent.ch joins Bent and Bench, saying plainly what has changed from an ordinary bench: the seat has been curved.

chapters.heading: Why the seat curves
body: The seat curves through roughly 120 degrees and is only 180 mm across. Sitting down, weight goes into the thighs rather than the backside, so the sitter holds their own back straight and can stretch their legs out.
The bench is deliberately not too comfortable. It is meant as a short rest, so that when one person is done there is room for the next, rather than somewhere to settle for the afternoon.
points: Can be sat on along the bench or across it
Seven parts: one seat and two legs, quick to assemble
Slender enough to take up little floor

chapters.heading: Where it goes
body: The bench was designed for a range of settings: schoolyards, parks, libraries and front porches. In a school or park it is somewhere to rest; in a library it becomes a reading chair.

chapters.heading: Exhibited
body: Bent.ch was built at full scale and shown at SEE+ Design Fair 2023, organised by C.space Design Complex with Van Lang University.
